ownership_reason: Only the gold decides, for a class that is not an array, which type the factory constructs (a MapType for a Map class, a CollectionType for a Collection class, a simple type otherwise) and checks the parameter count each container kind needs; hop 1 answers only array classes and hops 2-4 pass the receiver and the three values on unchanged. The gold's javadoc promises the JavaType that represents the parameterized type; for Map<String,ArrayList<String>> that type is a MapType in Jackson's type model, and the variant returns a SimpleType. No one-line change of the values above the gold makes it return a MapType (it sends every non-Collection class to constructSimpleType), and recovering after the gold cannot produce the trigger's 'Need exactly 2 parameter types for Map types' for a Map class with one parameter, for which the gold's simple path already throws its own mismatch message. The convention is pinned outside the gold: TypeFactory._fromClass builds a Map class through _mapType as MapType.construct, and the generic-aware TypeFactory._fromParameterizedClass and _fromParamType build a Map class with type parameters as MapType.construct(raw, key, value) (a Collection class as CollectionType); TestTypeFactory::testMaps (raw HashMap, constructMapType(TreeMap, ...) and TypeReference<HashMap<String,Integer>> all give MapType) and TestTypeFactory::testCollections pass, and TestWithGenerics::testWrapperWithExplicitType and TestTypedContainerSerialization::testIssue329 pass through the whole chain.
